plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and the payment rule (paying the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, a reasonable expectation for the second-highest bid is around $10. However, my value is $22, significantly higher than the upper bound. I will bid a small increment above $10 to ensure winning while minimizing payment.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately 2/3 * 20 = $13.33. To maximize profit and win, I should bid just above this. However, my value is $23, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid $13.40 to ensure I win against bids below that.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the item to a slightly higher bid, resulting in a loss of potential profit. Any bid above your value risks overpaying. Since there's only one round, there's no long-term strategy to consider. Therefore, I will bid my value.
